description: Redis password generation drift caused by Helm include re-evaluation producing a different random password at every call site
_fidelity: Rebuilt from source at the pinned SHA. The previous key was 1-of-3 correct: it named templates/health-configmap.yaml and templates/master/application.yaml as drift points, and NEITHER contains a call to the redis.password helper (verified: `include "redis.password"` occurs 0 times in each). health-configmap.yaml reads the password at container RUNTIME from $REDIS_PASSWORD_FILE, and master/application.yaml consumes the secret by reference — neither can drift at template time. Both real call sites were missing: templates/secret-svcbind.yaml (the ServiceBinding — the mismatch PR #36231's title actually names) and templates/configmap.yaml. The old key was also internally inconsistent: its root_cause prose said 'the ServiceBinding resource' while its drift_points array listed master/application.yaml instead. Its root_cause further claimed _helpers.tpl 'calls randAlphaNum on every invocation'; randAlphaNum occurs 0 times in redis/_helpers.tpl — the randomness is one level down in the common subchart.
root_cause: Helm re-evaluates a named template on every {{ include }}. The redis.password helper (bitnami/redis/templates/_helpers.tpl:206-210) does not itself randomise: it delegates to common.secrets.passwords.manage in the common subchart (bitnami/common/templates/_secrets.tpl), which calls randAlphaNum when no password is provided and no existing secret is found. Because each include re-runs that path, every call site materialises a DIFFERENT random password. PR #36231 fixes it by memoising the first result into .Values.global.redis.password and returning that thereafter.

scenario.values: serviceBindings.enabled=true, auth.password unset; all else default (auth.enabled=true, auth.acl.enabled=false, auth.existingSecret unset, auth.usePasswordFileFromSecret=true)
scenario.note: The rendered call sites — and therefore the drift points — depend on this scenario. Verified against the guards at the pinned SHA.

drift_points.renders_when: auth.enabled and not auth.existingSecret and (auth.usePasswordFileFromSecret or not auth.usePasswordFiles) — true under the scenario
drift_points.expected: the same generated password every other call site resolves to, memoised via global.redis.password
drift_points.actual: a fresh randAlphaNum value, because this include re-runs common.secrets.passwords.manage

drift_points.renders_when: serviceBindings.enabled — set true by the scenario
drift_points.expected: the same generated password the Secret holds, so the ServiceBinding authenticates
drift_points.actual: a second, unrelated randAlphaNum value — the mismatch reported in #15626 and fixed by PR #36231

not_drifted.note: A REAL third call site ({{- $password := include "redis.password" . }}) but gated by auth.acl.enabled, which defaults to false — it does not render under this scenario. Credit it if the scenario ever enables ACL; do not grade it now.
Named by the OLD key and wrong: 0 calls to redis.password. Reads the password at container runtime from $REDIS_PASSWORD_FILE, so it cannot drift at template time.
Named by the OLD key and wrong: 0 calls to redis.password. Consumes the secret by reference (volume name / mount path), so it cannot drift at template time.

fix_approach: Memoise: store the generated password in .Values.global.redis.password on the first call and return it on subsequent calls, so every include resolves to the same value (PR #36231).

scoring_evidence._comment: Tokens absent from instruction.md (verified with fixed-string grep -coF). The prompt DOES supply 'redis.password' (2), 'serviceBindings.enabled' (2), '_helpers.tpl' (1), 'ServiceBinding' (1) and the whole re-evaluation story, so none of those may be graded. It never names common.secrets.passwords.manage, randAlphaNum, global.redis.password or secret-svcbind.yaml — reaching those requires opening the chart and following the helper into the common subchart.

verification.method: gh_api_pr_files + raw source at pinned SHA

Guards checked against values.yaml defaults: auth.enabled=true, auth.acl.enabled=false, auth.usePasswordFileFromSecret=true, serviceBindings.enabled=false (set true by the scenario). randAlphaNum: 0 hits in redis/_helpers.tpl; the helper delegates to common.secrets.passwords.manage at _helpers.tpl:208. Pinned SHA is dated one day before PR #36231 merged, so the buggy state is present.
